actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The observation is a 26-element flat vector: position error (3), orientation quaternion xyzw (4), linear velocity (3), angular velocity (3), depth error (1), roll and pitch heading error (2), the previous six-dimensional action (6) and the previous hydro wrench (4)
The observation space is an unbounded 26-element Box and the action space is a 6-element Box with element-wise bounds -1.0 and +1.0
The action is a six-degree-of-freedom wrench command (surge, sway, heave, roll, pitch, yaw) in [-1, +1] per DOF, mapped to the thrusters through the T_matrix pseudoinverse
The default integration step is DEFAULT_DT = 1/240 s
ROVEnv's dt argument defaults to DEFAULT_DT
init_pos_noise_std and init_yaw_noise_std are uniform half-ranges, not standard deviations

A reset samples a position offset per axis uniformly in [-init_pos_noise_std, +init_pos_noise_std] and a yaw offset uniformly in [-init_yaw_noise_std, +init_yaw_noise_std] with the environment's np_random generator
reset() seeds the environment's np_random generator through gymnasium's Env.reset
The default target position is [0.0, 0.0, -1.5] m
A reset option target_position replaces the target position
The episode truncates when the step count reaches max_episode_steps
The episode terminates when the ROV is more than 5.0 m from its target
step always returns batched shapes: observation (n_envs, 26) and reward and flags (n_envs,)
The environment adds Gaussian noise of sensor_noise_std to every observation entry, drawn from torch.randn_like rather than the seeded generator
Each environment models one free-body sphere (an ROV proxy) with 6-DOF hydrodynamic forces computed by the Tier-1 kernels
OceanScale is an alpha GPU-native underwater-robotics simulator built on Newton and Warp
An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.8+ is required and Linux x86_64 is the supported platform
The install pulls CUDA-enabled wheels of warp-lang, newton and torch

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the reset-noise generator, but the upstream observation adds unseeded Gaussian sensor noise (rov_env.py:768-769), so repeated runs with one seed do not produce equal state hashes; the package's fake omits the sensor noise and is deterministic for a seed, which is a property of the fake, not a claim about the upstream simulator

gaps: rigid-body hydrodynamics of one sphere per environment: no contact, thruster or actuator fidelity claim, and no claim that the Fossen coefficients match a physical BlueROV2
the fake backend replaces Newton, Warp, Torch and Tier-1 hydrodynamics with a kinematic acceleration and linear drag (fake.py), so its trajectories are not the upstream ones
the fake models one environment and returns a flat 26-vector and scalar reward; upstream's step always returns batched (n_envs, 26) arrays and the constructor default is n_envs=64
upstream adds Gaussian sensor noise to every observation entry (rov_env.py:768-769); the fake omits it, so the fake is deterministic for a seed while the upstream simulator is statistical
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the simulator was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
